  "confidence": 0.45,
  "anomalies": [
    {
      "category": "wrong_component_type",
      "components": ["Q1", "U6", "J3"],
      "pins": ["Q1.2", "Q1.3", "U6.1", "U6.6"],
      "nets": ["+5V", "USBC_VBUS_IN"],
      "observed": "Q1 (AO3401A P-channel MOSFET, Q_PMOS_GSD) has its source (pin 2, S) on +5V and its drain (pin 3, D) on USBC_VBUS_IN. U6 (LTC4412, ideal-diode OR-ing controller) has VIN (pin 1) on USBC_VBUS_IN and SENSE (pin 6) on +5V. The controller's own SENSE pin is on the +5V output side, but the pass FET is oriented with its drain on the input side.",
      "expected": "In an LTC4412 ideal-diode arrangement the P-channel pass device conducts from the input (VIN, here USBC_VBUS_IN) to the load, so its source should be on the VBUS input and its drain on +5V. Its body diode should block reverse flow from the 5 V rail back to USB VBUS.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"Q1\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"S\") (pintype \"passive\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"Q1\") (pin \"3\") (pinfunction \"D\") (pintype \"passive\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"U6\") (pin \"1\") (pinfunction \"VIN\") (pintype \"power_in\"))"},
        {"source": "spec", "quote": "USB input \"OR-ing\"/protection circuitry (LTC4412 ideal-diode controller, `U6`)"},
        {"source": "spec", "quote": "need reverse current protection mostly"}
      ],
      "impact": "The pass FET is inverted relative to the controller's intended topology. Reverse-current protection fails, and the 5 V rail can backfeed the USB input, or the USB path does not behave as an ideal diode.",
      "confidence": 0.45
    },
    {
      "category": "bridged_nets",
      "components": ["D30", "R60", "R59"],
      "pins": ["D30.4", "D30.2", "R60.1", "R60.2"],
      "nets": ["ESTOP_OUT", "Net-(D30-K2)"],
      "observed": "The second LED channel of dual LED D30 has its anode (pin 4, A2) on ESTOP_OUT. Its cathode (pin 2, K2) goes through series resistor R60 back to ESTOP_OUT. The LED therefore sits across a loop with both ends on the same node and cannot conduct. The other channel (A1 on the 3.3 V LED net, K1 through R59 to GND) is wired correctly.",
      "expected": "The indicator LED should be driven from the 3.3 V LED supply (LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV) through its series resistor R60 to ESTOP_OUT, so that ESTOP_OUT low lights the LED. Its anode should not be on the signal it is meant to sense.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"D30\") (pin \"4\") (pinfunction \"A2\") (pintype \"input\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"R60\") (pin \"2\") (pintype \"passive\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"D30\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"K2\") (pintype \"input\"))"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R60 Net-_D30-K2_ ESTOP_OUT 130"}
      ],
      "impact": "The E-stop status LED on channel 2 never lights, and the series resistor R60 is effectively a short loop. This gives a misleading status indication for the e-stop output.",
      "confidence": 0.35
    },
    {
      "category": "wrong_value",
      "components": ["R36"],
      "pins": ["R36.1", "R36.2"],
      "nets": ["VOUTN", "VOUTP"],
      "observed": "R36 is valued \"24k\" in the netlist and the SPICE deck, but the placed part is MPN FRC0805J240TSD with description \"125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805\". The part code and description both indicate 24 Ω, not 24 kΩ.",
      "expected": "A 24 kΩ value (as drawn) should be sourced as a 24 kΩ part, for example a 243 code rather than 240. A 24 Ω part across the high-voltage output would dissipate far more than its 125 mW rating.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(comp (ref \"R36\") (value \"24k\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(field (name \"MPN\") \"FRC0805J240TSD\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "\" 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS\""},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R36 VOUTN VOUTP 24k"}
      ],
      "impact": "If the 24 Ω part is fitted, it loads the VOUTP/VOUTN output with a large current, overheating and possibly destroying the resistor. Output regulation and the output-stage behaviour also change.",
      "confidence": 0.3
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The SPICE deck matches the netlist, so the findings come from the netlist. The most suspicious items are the reversed pass-FET orientation of Q1 relative to the LTC4412 ideal-diode arrangement, the LED D30 channel 2 anode tied to its own ESTOP_OUT loop, and R36 being valued 24k while the placed part is a 24 Ω MPN. Confidence is moderate because the reference design may share some of these properties."
}

anomalies.observed: Q1 (AO3401A P-channel MOSFET, Q_PMOS_GSD) has its source (pin 2, S) on +5V and its drain (pin 3, D) on USBC_VBUS_IN. U6 (LTC4412, ideal-diode OR-ing controller) has VIN (pin 1) on USBC_VBUS_IN and SENSE (pin 6) on +5V. The controller's own SENSE pin is on the +5V output side, but the pass FET is oriented with its drain on the input side.
anomalies.expected: In an LTC4412 ideal-diode arrangement the P-channel pass device conducts from the input (VIN, here USBC_VBUS_IN) to the load, so its source should be on the VBUS input and its drain on +5V. Its body diode should block reverse flow from the 5 V rail back to USB VBUS.
anomalies.impact: The pass FET is inverted relative to the controller's intended topology. Reverse-current protection fails, and the 5 V rail can backfeed the USB input, or the USB path does not behave as an ideal diode.

anomalies.observed: The second LED channel of dual LED D30 has its anode (pin 4, A2) on ESTOP_OUT. Its cathode (pin 2, K2) goes through series resistor R60 back to ESTOP_OUT. The LED therefore sits across a loop with both ends on the same node and cannot conduct. The other channel (A1 on the 3.3 V LED net, K1 through R59 to GND) is wired correctly.
anomalies.expected: The indicator LED should be driven from the 3.3 V LED supply (LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV) through its series resistor R60 to ESTOP_OUT, so that ESTOP_OUT low lights the LED. Its anode should not be on the signal it is meant to sense.
anomalies.impact: The E-stop status LED on channel 2 never lights, and the series resistor R60 is effectively a short loop. This gives a misleading status indication for the e-stop output.

anomalies.observed: R36 is valued "24k" in the netlist and the SPICE deck, but the placed part is MPN FRC0805J240TSD with description "125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805". The part code and description both indicate 24 Ω, not 24 kΩ.
anomalies.expected: A 24 kΩ value (as drawn) should be sourced as a 24 kΩ part, for example a 243 code rather than 240. A 24 Ω part across the high-voltage output would dissipate far more than its 125 mW rating.

evidence.quote: " 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS"

anomalies.impact: If the 24 Ω part is fitted, it loads the VOUTP/VOUTN output with a large current, overheating and possibly destroying the resistor. Output regulation and the output-stage behaviour also change.
